(Naperville, Illinois) | college = [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale]] (2021–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team1 = [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|end}}–present | team2 = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]]–present | team3 = →[[Texas Legends]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[Ivy League]] (2025) * Second-team All-Ivy League (2024) * [[Ivy League men's basketball tournament|Ivy League tournament]] MVP ([[2025 Ivy League men's basketball tournament|2025]]) }} '''John Michael Poulakidas''' (born April 4, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a two-way contract with the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale Bulldogs]]. ==High school career== Poulakidas attended [[Neuqua Valley High School]] in [[Naperville, Illinois]].{{Cite web |date=March 5, 2020 |title=Lockdown defense, John Poulakidas' shooting touch lead Neuqua Valley past Lockport |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2020/3/4/21165734/john-poulakidas-neuqua-valley-basketball |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=Chicago Sun-Times |language=en}} As a junior, he averaged 17.5 points and 4.6 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |last=Rudnik |first=Jakub |date=September 20, 2020 |title=Neuqua Valley's John Poulakidas Chooses Yale over Power 5 |url=https://illinois-basketball.com/neuqua-valley-john-poulakidas-commitment-yale/ |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=Illinois High School Basketball |language=en-US}} He committed to play college basketball at [[Yale University]] over offers from [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]], [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]], and [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]].{{Cite web |last=LeGrand |first=Ben |title=John Poulakidas announces long-awaited commitment for basketball |url=https://nvhsecho.com/2714/profiles/john-poulakidas-announces-long-awaited-commitment-for-basketball/ |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=The Echo}}{{Cite web |date=September 22, 2020 |title=Neuqua Valley's John Poulakidas makes a wise choice for basketball, committing to 'forty not four' in Ivy League power Yale |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/09/22/neuqua-valleys-john-poulakidas-makes-a-wise-choice-for-basketball-committing-to-forty-not-four-in-ivy-league-power-yale/ |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US}} ==College career== After playing sparingly as a freshman, Poulakidas started every game as a sophomore and junior.{{Cite web |last=Blouin |first=Drew |date=July 6, 2024 |title=Fitting in: Neuqua Valley graduate John Poulakidas hangs with elite college wings at Jayson Tatum camp |url=https://www.dailyherald.com/20240706/pro-sports/fitting-in-neuqua-valley-graduate-john-poulakidas-hangs-with-elite-college-wings-at-jayson-tatum-ca/ |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=Daily Herald |language=en-US}} As a junior in the first round of the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] against [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], he scored 28 points, making six three-pointers and helping lead Yale to a 78–76 upset victory.{{Cite news |last=Aldam |first=Will |title=Who is John Poulakidas? A look at Yale's NCAA first round hero |url=https://www.ctpost.com/sports/article/yale-basketball-john-poulakidas-march-madness-19364156.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240407184900/https://www.ctpost.com/sports/article/yale-basketball-john-poulakidas-march-madness-19364156.php |archive-date=April 7, 2024 |access-date=February 16, 2025 |work=Connecticut Post |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Botte |first=Peter |date=March 23, 2024 |title=Who is John Poulakidas? Yale folk hero led upset win over Auburn |url=https://nypost.com/2024/03/22/sports/who-is-john-poulakidas-yale-folk-hero-led-upset-win-over-auburn/ |access-date=February 16, 2025 |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Kennedy |first=Joe |date=November 19, 2024 |title=Naperville's John Poulakidas rises to the national spotlight with Yale Basketball |url=https://www.nctv17.org/sports/napervilles-john-poulakidas-rises-to-the-national-spotlight-with-yale-basketball/ |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=NCTV17 |language=en-US}} Poulakidas returned for his senior season, emerging as the team's leading scorer by averaging 19.4 points per game.{{Cite web |date=February 11, 2025 |title=Dom Amore: John Poulakidas keeps taking his best shots and Yale men's basketball is surging again |url=https://www.courant.com/2025/02/11/dom-amore-john-poulakidas-keeps-taking-his-best-shots-and-yale-mens-basketball-is-surging-again/ |access-date=February 16, 2025 |website=Hartford Courant |language=en-US}} ==Professional career== Poulakidas was not selected in the [[2025 NBA draft]]. He signed an [[NBA Summer League]] contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{Cite web |last = Cornwell | first = Justin |date=June 27, 2025 |title=Neuqua Valley alum John Poulakidas signs NBA summer league contract with the Los Angeles Clippers |url=https://www.nctv17.org/community-sports/neuqua-valley-alum-john-poulakidas-signs-nba-summer-league-contract-with-the-los-angeles-clippers/amp/ |access-date=June 30, 2025 |website=nctv17.com |language=en-US}} On March 3, 2026, Poulakidas signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web|title=The Dallas Mavericks Sign John Poulakidas To A Two-Way Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/the-dallas-mavericks-sign-john-poulakidas-to-a-two-way-contract|date=March 3, 2026|access-date=March 3, 2026|website=gleague.nba.com}} Immediately after his signing, that same day, he made his NBA debut, playing 14 minutes and 28 seconds of game time action in a 90–117 loss against the [[2025–26 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]]; he grabbed five rebounds and dished out two assists.{{cite web |title=Poulakidas makes NBA debut for Dallas Mavericks, playing 14 minutes|url=https://yaledailynews.com/articles/poulakidas-makes-nba-debut-for-dallas-mavericks-playing-14-minutes |website=[[Yale Daily News]] |access-date=April 13, 2026 }} On April 12, Poulakidas put up a career-high 28 points in a 149–128 win over the [[2025–26 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/dallas-mavericks/mavericks-news-ryan-nembhard-passes-jason-kidd-all-time-franchise-rookie-record|title=Mavericks’ Ryan Nembhard passes Jason Kidd for all-time franchise rookie record|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pereira|first=Richard|date=April 12, 2026|access-date=April 12, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1955431/john-poulakidas-luka-garza-clint-capela-nba-european-recap/|title=Poulakidas, Garza, Capela excel as the NBA Regular Season concludes|website=Eurohoops|date=April 13, 2026|access-date=April 13, 2026}} On July 3, 2026, it was announced that Poulakidas would be participating with the Mavericks in the [[2026 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |last=Curtis |first=Mike |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/article/summer-league-roster-morez-johnson-nembhard-sergio-22331856.php |title=Mavericks reveal Summer League roster featuring Morez Johnson, Ryan Nembhard Jr., Sergio de Larrea |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |date=July 3, 2026 |access-date=July 3, 2026}} ==Personal life== Poulakidas's parents are both Greek. "My father's parents are from Greece, my grandfather was born in [[Sparta, Laconia|Sparta]], and grandmother is from the island of [[Chios]]. On my mom's side, both parents are from the [[Peloponnese]], from a village called [[Rizes]]. All my grandparents are Greek, all my family and ancestry are Greek. I speak a little Greek, but I haven't learned it very well," he revealed in an interview with [[ERT3]].{{Cite web |date=May 28, 2024 |title=Mavericks' John Poulakidas: The Greek-American who drove the NCAA "crazy" may get a Greek passport |url=https://www.newgreektv.com/news-in-english-for-greeks/omogeneia/item/36492-the-greek-american-who-drove-the-ncaa-crazy-gets-a-greek-passport-and-dreams-of-olympiakos-or-panathinaikos|access-date=March
